newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL- KEY THROWS SIX-HIT SHUTOUT AS ORIOLES BEAT RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL- KEY THROWS SIX-HIT SHUTOUT AS ORIOLES BEAT RANGERS.

text.p: Jimmy Key pitched a six-hit shutout and Jeffrey Hammonds hit a pair of solo homers as the Baltimore Orioles improved upon the American League's best record with a 9-0 rout of the Texas Rangers Sunday.

Key (2-0) walked one and struck out seven in his first shutout since May 28, 1993 for the Yankees against the White Sox. He improved to 6-1 lifetime at Camden Yards, where he has allowed seven earned runs and 36 hits over seven starts and 50 1/3 innings (1.25 ERA).
Key, who threw 122 pitches, recorded his 13th career shutout and 34th complete game.

"The important thing is that I got up to 120 pitches, which is a good sign," Key said. "My arm is healthy and I feel pretty good. We got ahead early and I was able to keep the ball down and in the park. I had the ball moving low today. When I do that I am usually in control."
"He's awesome, he made good pitches, good location, kept them off-balance," said catcher Chris Hoiles.
Rafael Palmeiro had four singles for Baltimore (7-2), which has won three straight. The Orioles have won four of five meetings with Texas this season.
"The guys have just been doing what they are capable of doing," manager Davey Johnson said. "We're an explosive ballclub. It's fun to see good defence and good pitching."
Cal Ripken and Hoiles also homered for Baltimore.
Roger Pavlik (1-1) took the loss.
In Boston, Tim Naehring hit a grand slam and Tom Gordon allowed one unearned run over eight innings as the Red Sox beat the Mariners 7-1, ending Seattle's four-game win streak.
Wil Cordero added a solo home run and Mike Stanley doubled in a run for Boston, which snapped a three-game losing streak.
Gordon (1-1) gave up four hits and struck out six in eight innings as he improved to 13-4 lifetime against Seattle. Heathcliff Slocumb pitched a scoreless ninth.
Scott Sanders (0-3) allowed six runs and seven hits over four innings.
In Cleveland, Darin Erstad and Jim Edmonds each scored a run and drove in another as the Anaheim Angels again pounded Jack McDowell in an 8-3 victory over the Indians.
Erstad had three hits, Edmonds had a pair and Garret Anderson also had two hits and scored a run.
Former Indian Eddie Murray hit his 502nd career homer in the fourth for Anaheim, which collected 13 hits and earned a split of the rain-shortened series.
Mark Langston (1-1) notched his first win against the Indians since May 1, 1992. McDowell (0-1) was hit hard for the second time in as many starts this season.
In Milwaukee, Fernando Vina singled home Gerald Williams with no outs in the bottom of the ninth inning, lifting the Brewers to a 3-2 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays.

Williams, who went 3-for-4, led off the ninth against Tim Crabtree (0-1) with a flare to shallow right that he stretched into a double. Jesse Levis reached on an error by second baseman Carlos Garcia while sacrificing Williams to third and Vina singled to right on a 1-0 pitch, scoring the winning run.
Bob Wickman (1-0) pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings for the victory.
In Detroit, the Tigers and Chicago White Sox split a twin bill.
Albert Belle scored on a wild pitch by John Cummings and Norberto Martin had a two-run single in the 12th as the White Sox erased a seven-run deficit to win the opener 11-8.
Belle was walked by Felipe Lira (0-1), who took the loss.
Roberto Hernandez blew the save but got the win. He yielded a game-tying home run to Travis Fryman after Vince Coleman was picked off first in the 11th.
In the nightcap, Fryman hit a three-run homer with one out in the bottom of the ninth to salvage a split for the Tigers with a 4-2 win.
Hernandez (1-1) blew his second save opportunity of the day to take the loss.
In New York, the Yankees and Oakland Athletics split a doubleheader.
Bernie Williams and Derek Jeter homered in support of Andy Pettitte as the Yankees eked out a 3-2 victory in the opener.
Pettitte (3-0), who improved to 16-3 in the last two seasons after Yankees losses, gave up a run and four hits with three walks and four strikeouts in seven innings.
Dave Telgheder (0-1) took the loss.
In the nightcap, Geronimo Berroa got four hits and Scott Brosius keyed a four-run third inning with a two-run single as Oakland beat the Yankees 7-4.
Berroa went 5-for-8 in the two games, raising his career average against the Yankees to .362 (55-for-152) with 13 homers and 40 RBI.

In Kansas City, Johnny Damon and David Howard, the eighth and ninth batters in the order, each drove in three runs and Kevin Appier (1-0) yielded five hits over eight strong innings as the Royals defeated the Minnesota Twins 6-1.
